acceptance_criteria.criterion: Evaluate(Parse("Rating >= 4"), item) returns true for Rating = 5 and false for Rating = 3.
Evaluate(Parse("NeedsReview()"), item) returns true when item.NeedsReview == true and false otherwise.
Evaluate(Parse("ActorsContain(\"smith\")"), item) returns true when item.ActorNames contains "Smith" (case-insensitive).
Evaluate(Parse("HasThumbnails()"), item) returns true when item.ThumbnailCount > 0 and false when zero.
Evaluate(Parse("NOT NeedsReview()"), item) returns the logical inverse of NeedsReview().
Evaluate(Parse("Rating >= 4 AND HasBookmarks()"), item) requires both conditions true.
Evaluate(Parse("Rating < 2 OR NeedsReview()"), item) is true if either condition holds.
Evaluate(Parse("AmountTags = 0"), item) returns true for an item with TagCount == 0.
All numeric comparisons operate in decimal space — no double promotion occurs.
Zero new NuGet dependencies; only BCL types used.

comments.note: FilterExpressionEvaluator.EvaluateFunction uses a chain of string.Equals checks (OrdinalIgnoreCase) for function dispatch. This is fine for the current M5 set (~8 functions). If the function set grows significantly in later milestones, a Dictionary<string, Func<FunctionCallNode, MovieListItem, bool>> dispatch table would eliminate the linear scan and make it easier to register new functions.

comments.note: AND/OR short-circuit behaviour is verified via a test that places an unknown identifier on the right side of a short-circuiting expression. If the C# && / || short-circuit were ever replaced with eager evaluation, those tests would start throwing and catch the regression immediately.

EvaluateStringContains validates exactly one string argument and throws FilterExpressionException if the count or type is wrong. No test was written for the wrong-argument path because the parser already rejects non-string arguments to ActorsContain/StudioContains at parse time. If runtime argument injection becomes possible (e.g., programmatic AST construction), a targeted test for the argument-validation branch would be worth adding.
No improvement on the implementation beyond what was already observed by the Developer — the linear if-chain for function dispatch is acceptable at M5 scale.

summary: Code review PASS. Reviewed FilterExpressionEvaluator.cs and FilterExpressionEvaluatorTests.cs. No blocking issues found. All 10 acceptance criteria independently verified against the implementation.

FilterExpressionEvaluator is correctly designed as a sealed, static-only class. Switch expression on node type is exhaustive. Decimal promotion from int property values is implicit and safe — no double path exists. EvaluateStringContains validates argument count and type.
Short-circuit evaluation naturally delegated to C# && / || operators. Tests use an unreachable IdentifierNode right-hand side to verify no evaluation occurs — clever and robust.
All MovieListItem string properties used in EvaluateStringContains (ActorNames, Studio) are required string — no null dereference risk.
Test quality is high: 57 tests covering all ACs, all 8 functions, all 6 comparison operators, short-circuit AND/OR, double-NOT identity, null guards, and error paths.

comments.note: FilterExpressionEvaluator is correctly designed as a static-only utility class (sealed, private constructor). No issues.
